title: Recording: Ram On, Now Hear This Song Of Mine by Paul and Linda McCartney | 1971
content:
Studio A-1, A&R Recording, New York City
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Dixon Van Winkle

Paul McCartney recorded ‘Ram On’, and its reprise later on in the Ram album, on 22 February 1971. It was McCartney’s first new song recorded since November 1970.

Before that, though, he worked on ‘Now Hear This Song Of Mine’. McCartney had the idea to use the track for radio spots to promote Ram. He filled two tape reels with versions of the song, accompanying himself on piano. He continued work on the piece on 1 March.

‘Ram On’ was recorded late at night, following a review of the album’s progress so far.

We’d worked a lot of the day, I guess, and there was nobody there, everybody had gone. It was like midnight or something, and Paul said, ‘Can you set me up in the studio? I want to record a ukulele.’

I put a mic on each of his feet, and a vocal mic, and two on his ukulele, and that was it. I just hit the record button, and he came out with ‘Ram On’. It was kind of a magic moment, so personal. And the beauty of it was, it was take one!

Dixon Van Winkle, 2017
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73, Allan Kozinn, Adrian Sinclair

Later in the week McCartney added a second ukulele part, and overdubbed a rhythm on a tom tom, then he and Linda McCartney overdubbed backing vocals.

Studio engineer Dixon Van Winkle had previously compiled the best takes from McCartney’s masters of the New York Ram sessions. He then added ‘Ram On’ to one of the four tapes, using some discarded tape as leader. By chance, the tape reel had previously contained some piano music, not played by McCartney, which duly became the intro of the song.
